artist_scope: full contract (Tier 1, the simple-cyclic class: geckolib_migration_design.md section 5) with the §8.1 locks (none pre-declared: the design's section 6 keeps this consumer of the shared ButterflyModel single-box); the rig is not yet in-game (it lands through the seam in a later slice)
character_sheet: A hostile butterfly on the shared butterfly rig: a one-cube body bar, a one-cube head and four flat wing panels a side — inner and outer forewings, a hindwing and a long tail streamer (ButterflyModel.createBodyLayer, ButterflyModel.java:54-102) — in the vampire skin, a twin of the butterfly's (VampireButterflyRenderer.java:22-23). It is a Monster, not an ambient creature (VampireButterfly.java:56): it wanders on the butterfly flight preset (:79), takes revenge on whatever hurt it and targets the nearest player within 16 blocks (:80-81), then steers straight at its target each tick and bites within touch range (customServerAiStep :111-136) — 2.0 of damage, Hunger for 200 ticks, Weakness for 120, a small knockback, and an attacking-ticks pulse of 10 the model does not read (doHurtTarget :139-154). It whines the mosquito sound when hurt (:176-179), never takes fall damage (:161-168), and spawns under the light-free monster rule (:196-203) wherever a roster places it (no biome modifier or biome file names it in the port's data today). Read it as the butterfly with intent: the same flutter, but it homes in.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (VampireButterflyRenderer has no scale override; shadow 0.2, VampireButterflyRenderer.java:29) on the shared 64x32 sheet (ButterflyModel.java:104) in the vampire_butterfly.png skin (VampireButterflyRenderer.java:22-23); 0.5 x 0.5 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:667-668). The wing panels are one unit thick.

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) each way; the four left panels the negative of the four right panels
groups.plain: the eight wing panels flap about the body's long axis together, 45 degrees up and down, the left side mirroring the right; nothing else moves
groups.math: rightwing.zRot = rightwing2.zRot = rightwing3.zRot = rightwing4.zRot = cos(ageInTicks * 1.3 * 1.0) * pi * 0.25; leftwing*.zRot = -rightwing.zRot
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x wingspeed 1.0 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.3 = 4.83 ticks

behaviour: One rhythm runs at all times: the eight wing panels roll about the body's long axis at 1.3 rad/tick (a 4.83-tick beat), 45 degrees each way, the left set mirroring the right (ButterflyModel.java:109-115). The body and the head are static; the walk position, the walking speed, the head angles and the entity's state play no part — the model flaps the same wandering, chasing and biting.

The flight is the entity's: AmbientFlightGoal's butterfly preset wanders it (VampireButterfly.java:79) and, with a target, customServerAiStep adds a 0.04-per-tick step toward the target's eyes and damps the motion by 0.92 (:120-128), looking at the target (:129); tick :99-104 damps the vertical speed by 0.6. The bite lands when it is within 1.4 blocks plus half the target's width (:131-134).

The synced ATTACKING_TICKS integer (VampireButterfly.java:61-62) is set to 10 by a landed bite (:151) and counts down each tick (:105-107): a hit pulse the model does not read, and not the contract's DATA_ATTACKING byte.
The renderer draws the head, then the body, then the wing pairs inner to outer (renderToBuffer, ButterflyModel.java:119-130).

wishlist: in `fly`: a faster, jerkier bob than the ambient butterfly's — it homes in on players (VampireButterfly.java:120-129) and should read as hungry, not drifting
in `attack`: a lunge with the head cube leading and the wings snapped back for the bite (:139-154)
in `idle`: a nervous tremor of the wings between beats, so a hovering vampire reads differently from the ambient butterfly on the same rig
a tail-streamer lag: `leftwing4` / `rightwing4` trailing a few degrees behind the panels instead of rolling rigidly with them
locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ButterflyModel row (geckolib_migration_design.md:440) keeps this consumer single-box — 'vampire_butterfly [0.5,0.5] stay single-box', 'other shared-rig consumers get no profile' — so no intended locked bones are pre-declared; the row's four part bones (body, head, leftwing, rightwing) belong to mothra's profile only.
